Needs changes before merge.

The queue keeps all planned steps. Builds run first. The named isolated targets run alone. The executor reports failed suites and checkout changes.

Local results:
- The trial merge with upstream/main 983f527bd7aab4f856666e62f0c06f381bc57474 succeeded without conflicts.
- `cargo test -p xtask --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p xtask`: passed. There were 161 unit tests and 15 integration tests. No test failed.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`: passed. This command ran no test. Its merge-base selection also included changes from main.

Requested before merge:
1. PR body:1, for `xtask/src/queue.rs:24`: Add the exact line `Process change: yes`. Current upstream AGENTS.md requires this line for an xtask change. Keep `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` unchanged.
2. PR body, final line: Link the issue that tracks this work. End the PR body with `Fixes #N` for that issue. The PR has no linked closing issue. Current upstream AGENTS.md requires issue tracking and this closing reference.
3. `xtask/src/lanes.rs:17`: Add `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md` for the scheduling decisions. Record the choice, the reason, the rejected options, and the cost of a later change. The PR changes the isolation policy and the scheduler, but has no decision file. The body explains the design; the decision file is also required by current upstream AGENTS.md.

Notes:
- This PR changes only xtask. It changes no posted G-code, geometry, simulation, or collision check. It changes no golden file or UI file. Safety mutations and UI screenshots do not apply.
- I did not run a full release gate or measure the performance gain. The promised server measurements are not yet in the comments.
- I used no GitHub runner. I made no code change.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

The metadata pins were external checks. No review evidence was committed. PROCESS_VERSION is unchanged.

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

I am the independent review agent. I did not write this change.

The three findings from the earlier review are now met:
- The PR body has the exact line `Process change: yes`. The PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.
- The PR body ends with `Fixes #2466`. That issue tracks this work.
- `docs/decisions/2466-gate-release-lanes.md` records the choices, reasons, rejected options, and costs of later changes.

The queue keeps the planned steps. Builds run first and alone. UI tests, clippy, and the named isolated targets run alone. The job limits stay within the budget. The executor reports failed suites and checkout changes.

Local results:
- The trial merge with upstream/main `983f527bd7aab4f856666e62f0c06f381bc57474` succeeded without conflicts.
- `cargo test -p xtask --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p xtask`: passed. All 161 unit tests and 15 integration tests passed.
- The executor test checked concurrent execution, suite failure, build failure, and checkout changes. It passed.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`: passed. It selected the xtask tests. This command ran no test.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes:
- This PR changes no posted G-code, gouge check, collision check, stock simulation, or geometry. Safety mutations do not apply.
- This PR changes no UI file or golden file. Screenshots and golden comparisons do not apply.
- I did not repeat the author's metadata mutations. I checked the resulting body, issue, and decision file directly.
- I did not run the full release gate or measure the performance gain. The server measurements remain unverified.
- I used no GitHub runner. I made no code change.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Measured: release gate before and after this PR** (`cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16`, under `xvfb-run`)

| | Before (main + #468, `199314e23`) | After (this PR, `ea0646853`) |
|---|---|---|
| Machine | 16 dedicated vCPU cloud server, warm sccache | 16-thread Ryzen 3700X, sccache off |
| Gate wall time | **114.6 min** | **77.0 min** (about 82 min with a cold debug build) |
| Steps | 1077, 1 failed | 1081, 0 failed |
| Summed step time | 147 min (1.3x the wall: mostly one core busy) | 427 min (5.5x the wall: the cores stay busy) |
| Debug / heavy build | 245 s / 259 s | 1 s (built by an earlier void run) / 292 s |
| Peak memory | - | 16.7 GB |

About one third less wall time, and the build phases are not the change. The new limit is the longest single steps: `motion suites: lib` 953 s, `app heavy: shared_face_bodies_finish` 878 s, `motion heavy: lib` 752 s. Under full load the steps take longer each (more contention), so a split of those three binaries is the next gain, not more jobs.

The two machines are not the same, so this is an estimate. A second "after" run on the cut runner's hardware type, with sccache, will follow.

The one failure in "before" was `ui` lib `setup_mount_pages::each_setup_picks_its_own_machine_and_post_and_posts_one_file_per_mount` (`Harness::run exceeded max_steps (4)`, a scroll area repaint). It passed in "after". It looks timing-dependent; it is watched, not filed yet.

**Third run: this PR on the cut runner's machine** (`uma`, 16 threads, sccache on, same head `ea0646853`; the runner was idle at the start and took a job before the end).

| | Before (cloud, #468) | After (dude) | After (uma) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gate wall time | 114.6 min | 77.0 min | **66.6 min** |
| Debug / heavy build | 245 s / 259 s | 1 s (warm) / 292 s | 577 s / 385 s (cold `target/`) |
| Summed step time | 147 min | 427 min | 282 min |

So on the cut runner the gate goes from about 2 h to about 1 h, and about 16 of the 67 minutes are the cold build.

Two failures in this run, neither from this PR:
- `clippy -D warnings`: the account's toolchain was an older clippy (0.1.99) that flags code main's clippy (0.1.100) accepts. Updated; not a code problem.
- `ui` lib `spindle_row::the_feeds_tab_offers_the_spindle_speed_and_its_unit_switch` ("the switch shows surface speed"). Together with the `setup_mount_pages` failure in "before" this is the second ui lib test that fails once under load and passes elsewhere. #2432 (isolate live theme state between parallel unit tests) looks like the fix for this class.
